variants.title: Give each part its job
variants.context: Model explainability is the practice of producing evidence about how a model's inputs relate to one output. SHAP (SHapley Additive exPlanations) assigns additive feature contributions relative to a reference. LIME (Local Interpretable Model-agnostic Explanations) fits a simple surrogate around one example and uses that local approximation to describe the black-box model.
variants.prompt: From the lesson section “SHAP distributes a prediction difference”: match each part to its responsibility.

pairs.label: Local accuracy
pairs.detail: The base value plus all contributions should recover the explained model output within the method's numerical tolerance and on the same output scale.
pairs.explanation: The base value plus all contributions should recover the explained model output within the method's numerical tolerance and on the same output scale.

pairs.label: Missingness
pairs.detail: A feature that is absent from the modeled coalition contributes zero under the explainer's missing-feature semantics.
pairs.explanation: A feature that is absent from the modeled coalition contributes zero under the explainer's missing-feature semantics. Those semantics must match the data domain.

pairs.label: Consistency
pairs.detail: When a model changes so a feature's marginal contribution never decreases, a consistent attribution method should not assign that feature a smaller value.
pairs.explanation: When a model changes so a feature's marginal contribution never decreases, a consistent attribution method should not assign that feature a smaller value.

pairs.label: Reference dependence
pairs.detail: The same prediction can have different valid base values and contribution splits when the comparison population or feature-dependence rule changes.
pairs.explanation: The same prediction can have different valid base values and contribution splits when the comparison population or feature-dependence rule changes.

variants.hint: Give each part the one job only it can do, then rule out the rest. A plausible chart can be wrong for the decision.
variants.explanation: Each part has a distinct responsibility. pairs.label: Generate plausible neighbors

variants.prompt: From the lesson section “Treat SHAP and LIME as different evidence contracts”: match each part to its responsibility.

pairs.label: Specialized SHAP
pairs.detail: Prefer an exact or efficient model-specific method when supported.
pairs.explanation: Prefer an exact or efficient model-specific method when supported. Verify output scale, base value, additivity, feature dependence, and behavior after model-library upgrades.

pairs.label: Model-agnostic SHAP
pairs.detail: Use when additive semantics matter but only prediction queries are available.
pairs.explanation: Use when additive semantics matter but only prediction queries are available. Budget many evaluations and gate seed, sample, and background sensitivity.

pairs.label: LIME
pairs.detail: Use for a bounded local investigation with a meaningful interpretable representation.
pairs.explanation: Use for a bounded local investigation with a meaningful interpretable representation. Gate local fidelity and do not promote one surrogate into global importance.

pairs.label: Interpretable model
pairs.detail: Use a monotonic model, scorecard, small tree, rule list, or generalized additive model when the real requirement is stable, inspectable decision logic.
pairs.explanation: Use a monotonic model, scorecard, small tree, rule list, or generalized additive model when the real requirement is stable, inspectable decision logic.

variants.prompt: From the lesson section “Correlation, interaction, and causality need separate treatment”: match each part to its responsibility.

pairs.label: Correlated substitutes
pairs.detail: Income, occupation, location, and credit history may carry overlapping signal.
pairs.explanation: Income, occupation, location, and credit history may carry overlapping signal. Perturbing one independently can create unrealistic records or shift credit to its substitute.

pairs.label: Feature interactions
pairs.detail: A contribution can depend on other feature values.
pairs.explanation: A contribution can depend on other feature values. Inspect interaction values, grouped concepts, or targeted slices instead of assuming every effect is independent.

pairs.label: Proxy behavior
pairs.detail: A permitted feature can encode protected or sensitive information.
pairs.explanation: A permitted feature can encode protected or sensitive information. Attribution may reveal the proxy, but policy and fairness tests must decide whether its use is acceptable.

pairs.label: Actionable intervention
pairs.detail: To recommend a change, define a feasible intervention, hold the right variables fixed, estimate counterfactual outcomes, and validate the action through domain or experimental evidence.
pairs.explanation: To recommend a change, define a feasible intervention, hold the right variables fixed, estimate counterfactual outcomes, and validate the action through domain or experimental evidence.

pairs.label: Faithfulness
pairs.detail: Measure additive reconciliation for SHAP or weighted local fidelity for LIME, then run deletion, insertion, sensitivity, and counterexample probes where appropriate.
pairs.explanation: Measure additive reconciliation for SHAP or weighted local fidelity for LIME, then run deletion, insertion, sensitivity, and counterexample probes where appropriate.

pairs.label: Repeatability
pairs.detail: Compare signs, top-feature overlap, rank correlation, and value variance across seeds, sample budgets, nearby cases, and repeated service calls.
pairs.explanation: Compare signs, top-feature overlap, rank correlation, and value variance across seeds, sample budgets, nearby cases, and repeated service calls.

pairs.label: Semantic robustness
pairs.detail: Vary plausible backgrounds, feature groupings, dependence assumptions, and output scales.
pairs.explanation: Vary plausible backgrounds, feature groupings, dependence assumptions, and output scales. Document expected movement and block unexplained reversals.

pairs.label: Human usefulness
pairs.detail: Test comprehension, calibrated trust, review time, contest quality, and error discovery with the actual audience instead of measuring chart preference alone.
pairs.explanation: Test comprehension, calibrated trust, review time, contest quality, and error discovery with the actual audience instead of measuring chart preference alone.

Semantic robustness: Vary plausible backgrounds, feature groupings, dependence assumptions, and output scales.
